conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Pin Art
style.description: A giant pin-impression toy (pinscreen): a clear acrylic frame holding a dense grid of thousands of slim polished metal pins with domed heads, on a dark matte desk under a strong low raking key light and a soft coloured rim light, so any relief pushed into the pins reads as a field of bright pin heads and long shadows. Polished steel by default, brass and anodised colour finishes. Shapes are pressed through the field as a pure function of time: every pin's extension is sampled from a target height field built from text and icons (distance fields with a rounded bevel), a hand, a ball rolling underneath, ripples from a tap, bars rising as columns of pins, terrain or a bitmap; transitions morph between fields with a wave that travels across the grid (per-pin delay from position, eased, tiny overshoot, metallic settle) and pins drop back in a cascade. The camera orbits low so relief and shadows read.

bump.description: fine fbm noise: matte painted desk top

motion: Every pin's extension = a height sampled from the current target height field; nothing else moves the pins.
Morph: per-pin delay from its position (directional, radial or seeded random wave), then a closed-form spring with ~5 % overshoot and a metallic settle; held exactly once settled.
Cascade: pins drop back with a gravity fall and one tiny bounce, in a seeded or swept order.
Layers: a ball rolling under the field (a travelling spherical bump, max with the field) and ripples spreading from a tap (added, then gone).
Camera: orbits low so relief and long shadows read; holds still between morphs (thousands of glints compress badly in motion).

notes.mechanism: pins.js: h_i(t) = sum over steps of (target_k - target_k-1) * settle(t - t_k - delay_k,i) (closed-form spring or gravity drop), max with a rolling-ball bump, plus a tap ripple; per-pin delays from position (radial / directional / seeded random).
notes.sampleData: bar values are SAMPLE DATA placeholders
